column1: # scripts/mutation/ledger.tsv — the EXEMPTION LEDGER for surviving mutants (ADR-049).
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   relpath <TAB> line_sha12 <TAB> col <TAB> family <TAB> from>to <TAB> class <TAB> reason
# THE THIRD FIELD IS A COLUMN, NOT A LINE. `col` is the 1-based CODEPOINT column
# of the mutated token on the line `line_sha12` pins — the `21` in the first row
# below is column 21, not line 21. There is deliberately NO line field: a line
# number would rot silently on any insertion above the row, which is the exact
# failure content-pinning exists to prevent, and scripts/mutation_lint.sh has no
# way to detect that rot. Issue #20 read these numbers as file lines and
# concluded the column was harness-normalized. It is not — the engine's line
# numbers are real file lines, straight from `Code.string_to_quoted/2` with
# `columns: true`, and it is only the ledger that (deliberately) does not store
# them. To recover the absolute line for a row:
#   elixir scripts/mutation/mutate.exs list <relpath>
# and match on (col, family, from, to, line_sha12). A gate run prints every site
# as `<line>:<col>` for the same reason.
# CONTENT-PINNED, NOT LINE-PINNED. `line_sha12` is the first 12 hex of SHA-256
# over the exact source line the exemption excuses. Inserting lines above a
# justified survivor keeps the exemption valid; EDITING that line changes the
# hash, so the exemption stops matching and scripts/mutation_lint.sh fails it as
# STALE. An exemption therefore cannot outlive the code it was written about —
# which is the whole reason this file is safe to have at all.
# CLASS — exactly two are allowed:
#   EQUIVALENT    the mutation provably cannot change behaviour (an equivalent
#                 mutant). The reason must say WHY, specifically. This is the only
#                 class that is not a debt.
#   ACCEPTED_GAP  the mutation DOES change behaviour and no test catches it — a
#                 real hole, consciously deferred. The reason MUST carry a
#                 `ref=<id>` pointing at the ADR/backlog item that owns it.
#                 scripts/mutation_lint.sh refuses an ACCEPTED_GAP without a ref.
# There is no third class and no bare "won't fix": a survivor with no honest
# entry here fails the gate, which is the point.
# A run prints the exact ledger key for every survivor it finds — paste that,
# then add class + reason.
# Filed 2026-09-18 from the first tier-1 run (61 mutants, 42 killed, 17 survived,
# 2 build-refused). Six further survivors from that same run were CLOSED WITH TESTS
# rather than exempted (MG-01..MG-06) — see ADR-049 section 7.
# ── 2026-09-21: RE-REPLAYED AGAINST `main` @ f8fcd79 (issues #20, #21) ───────
# Issue #21 predicted 13 rows (MG-07..13, 15..18, 21, 22) would be OBSOLETE once
# PR #26's 13 fail-closed proofs merged. The full tier-1 replay on that merge
# commit says otherwise: 61 mutants, 42 killed, 17 ledger-exempt, 2
# build-refused, ZERO obsolete — `MUTATION GATE: ALL PASSED`. No row below is
# dead weight by this gate's own rule, so no row was removed.
# WHY the prediction missed, and it is not a nuance: PR #26 put its proofs in NEW
# files (samen_core/test/hardening/*_fail_closed_test.exs) and did NOT add them
# to the owning-test column of scripts/mutation/targets.tsv. Every mutant runs
# ONLY its target's declared owning tests (that is the attribution contract, not
# an implementation detail), so the gate never executes those suites and these
# mutants genuinely survive the tests that claim to guard these files. Proven,
# not assumed: re-running with a scratch targets.tsv whose owning-test column is
# UNION'd with the five hardening suites FAILS with 14 obsolete rows — the
# predicted 13 PLUS MG-19, the highest-severity row — and leaves MG-14, MG-20 and
# the EQUIVALENT row still surviving.
# So the stale record here was never the ledger; it is targets.tsv's owning-test
# column. Wiring the five hardening suites in is a gate-configuration change with
# a real per-mutant runtime cost and it is what settles these 14 rows in one move;
# it is an operator call, not a records edit, and is deliberately NOT made here.
# Until it is made, every row below is live and load-bearing.
# ── 2026-09-23: THE CHANGE WAS MADE — 14 ROWS REMOVED (issue #20, PR #51) ─────
# PR #51 made owning tests DECLARED ∪ DERIVED (back-reference + `# MUTATION_OWNS:`),
# so the hardening suites and gate_policy_test now run for their targets. The
# tier-1 replay then FAILED on exactly the 14 rows predicted above — MG-07..13,
# 15..19, 21, 22 — as obsolete (killed by their proofs), and they are deleted
# here. MG-19, the highest-severity row, is closed. What remains below is MG-14
# (EQUIVALENT), MG-20 and the EQUIVALENT same_org_fk row: the 3 survivors the same
# replay still reports ledger-exempt.
samen_core/lib/samen/vault/change.ex
column7: ADR-049#MG-14, reclassified from ACCEPTED_GAP per issue #20 — it is not a debt. ensure_subject_attr/2's already-has-a-pk clause can only diverge on an UPDATE, and on an update the cond's fallthrough force-changes the pk to the value it already holds, where Ash's force_change_attribute/3 deletes a no-op change — so no input can observe the mutation. Proof by attempt, not by argument: a candidate test was written, run WITH and WITHOUT the mutation, passed both ways, and was deleted rather than shipped (a test that cannot fail is the tautology this repo refuses). Closing it would need a lib change, not a test.

column7: ref=ADR-049#MG-20 SECOND HIGHEST. all_belongs_to/1 selects the relationships the cross-org FK guard validates; inverting the filter hands it every NON-belongs_to relationship instead, and the suite's cross-org refusal still passes. Either the refusal under test is produced by a different code path than the one it credits, or the validation is a no-op on the mutated set. Investigate before writing the test.

column7: load_uuid/1's guard `is_binary(bin) and byte_size(bin) == 16` has a catch-all sibling `defp load_uuid(other), do: other`. Widening to `or` admits binaries of other lengths into the clause, where Ecto.UUID.load/1 returns :error and the clause returns `bin` — byte-identical to what the catch-all returns. Non-binaries still fall through (byte_size/1 raises inside a guard, which reads as false). No input can observe a difference.
